summary: Defines a MIB for configuring and managing TN3270E servers. It provides generic support for both host and gateway TN3270E server implementations.

eli5.summary: TN3270E lets you use an old mainframe terminal from a modern network. This is a standard control panel for the servers that provide that.

questions: difference between host and gateway tn3270e server
how to manage tn3270e servers with snmp
subtitle: A standard SNMP control panel for the servers that connect 3270 mainframe terminal emulators to SNA hosts.

tldr.problem: TN3270E servers connect Telnet 3270 terminal emulators to SNA hosts, but each implementation was configured and monitored in its own way, and host and gateway designs differ greatly.
tldr.mechanism: The memo defines the TN3270E-MIB, an SMIv2 module with tables for server control, resource configuration and mappings between SNA resource names and client addresses.
tldr.outcome: Management stations get one generic way to configure and watch both host and gateway TN3270E servers, and later memos can extend the MIB, as RFC 2562 does for response times.

today: RFC 2561 is a Proposed Standard from April 1999 and the metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. RFC 2562 extends it with response time collection.

sections.title: What the MIB Is For
sections.content:
TN3270E, defined by RFC 2355, refers to the enhancements made to Telnet 3270 (TN3270) terminal emulation practices. A TN3270E server connects a Telnet client performing 3270 emulation to a target SNA host. It sits between a client-side network (client to server), which is typically TCP/IP but need not be, and an SNA network (server to host).

RFC 2561 defines a Management Information Base (MIB) for configuring and managing such servers. It is a product of the TN3270E Working Group and is meant to be extended by later memos; the abstract names response time collection as one example.
sections.eli5: A TN3270E server is a translator between a person's screen and a big old computer. This memo says how to build a standard control panel for that translator.

sections.title: Host and Gateway Servers
sections.content:
The MIB gives generic support for two kinds of server. A host TN3270E server is collocated with the SNA System Services Control Point (SSCP) for the dependent secondary logical units (SLUs) it hands out to clients. A gateway TN3270E server lives on an SNA node other than an SSCP: a type 2.0 node, a boundary-function-attached type 2.1 node, or an APPN node acting as a Dependent LU Requester (DLUR).

The RFC notes that these two designs typically differ greatly in internal implementation and system definition methods, which is why a common management model is useful. The MIB is defined primarily for TN3270E servers. A TN3270-only server is not explicitly addressed, because it is considered unlikely to implement this MIB.
sections.eli5: Some of these translators sit inside the big computer and some sit in a separate box. The control panel is built so it works for both kinds.

sections.title: Structure of the MIB
sections.content:
The TN3270E-MIB splits into three groups: server control, server resource configuration, and resource and client address mappings. Three further topics are covered in prose: advisory spin lock usage, row persistence and IANA considerations.

The server control group holds tn3270eSrvrConfTable, tn3270eSrvrPortTable and tn3270eSrvrStatsTable. The first is the primary table: each server has one entry, indexed by tn3270eSrvrConfIndex, and most other tables use that index first. Its objects set inactivity and Telnet Timing Mark parameters, start and stop the server remotely, and report whether it is a host or gateway type. The port table lists the local TCP ports a server uses, and the stats table gives usage statistics.

Resource configuration uses tn3270eClientGroupTable, tn3270eResPoolTable and tn3270eClientResMapTable. The first two define groups of client addresses and pools of resources, and the third maps a client group to a resource pool.
sections.eli5: The control panel has a main page with one row per server, plus pages for its doors (ports), its counters and rules about which user gets which seat.

sections.title: Names, Addresses and Mappings
sections.content:
Three tables map between SNA names and client addresses: tn3270eSnaMapTable, tn3270eResMapTable and tn3270eTcpConnTable. A server gives a client access to an SNA application by tying the client's TCP connection to a secondary LU at the server, which in turn has an SNA session with a primary LU running on an SNA host.

The SLU names used locally at the server are often different from the names used in the rest of the SNA network. The MIB calls these local names and SSCP-supplied names. The read-only tn3270eSnaMapTable links the two, and tn3270eResMapTable maps a resource name to a client's address.

The tn3270eTcpConnTable lists current TN3270 and TN3270E sessions. It uses IANATn3270eAddrType and Tn3270eAddress pairs instead of IpAddress so that both IPv4 and IPv6 are supported, and puts the remote address before the local address in the index so GET-NEXT can work from the remote pair alone.
sections.eli5: The same seat can have a nickname inside the building and a different official name outside. These tables are the phone book that matches nicknames, official names and who is sitting there.

sections.title: Spin Locks, Persistence and IANA
sections.content:
tn3270eConfSpinLock is an advisory lock that lets cooperating management applications coordinate changes to the configuration tables. Applications SHOULD use it when creating or altering entries, agents SHALL NOT enforce it, but agents MUST implement the object.

Five tables allow remote row creation through RowStatus. An implementation SHOULD NOT keep SNMP-created entries across reIPLs of the server, so that management applications see consistent persistence behavior. Initial and permanent configuration is expected to come from local, implementation-dependent configuration.

Several textual conventions, for function flags, address types, resource types and device types, are imported from a separate IANATn3270eTC-MIB module. This lets IANA add values without a new version of the RFC.
sections.eli5: If two people edit the same settings, a polite sign-in sheet helps them take turns, but nobody is forced to use it. Settings made through the panel are forgotten when the server restarts.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
Some management information in this MIB may be sensitive. Authentication of SNMP requests and controlled access SHOULD be used in such environments. Several objects allow writes or row creation, and allowing that in a non-secure environment can harm network operations.

Implementers are RECOMMENDED to consider seriously whether set operations or row creation should be allowed without at least authentication of the request origin. Without it, the RFC recommends that a listed set of objects be read-only, including tn3270eSrvrConfAdminStatus, tn3270eSrvrConfContact and the RowStatus objects.

For every table except tn3270eTcpConnTable, the first index identifies one server, which makes it easy to give different principals access to different servers. That policy is not possible for the TCP connection table.
sections.eli5: Anyone who can change the control panel could mess up the service, so only let people who have proven who they are touch the switches.
